question: A 65-year-old man on the ward with a tracheostomy needs suctioning. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give oxygen and explain the procedure to the client
option_2: Insert the suction catheter without any preparation
option_3: Suction continuously for a full minute
option_4: Do the suctioning while the client is asleep
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give oxygen and explain the procedure to the client

Clinical Rationale: Oxygen is given and the procedure explained before suctioning because the passage of the catheter reduces the oxygen supply.

Key Clue: before suctioning a tracheostomy in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Tracheal suctioning

Why Not Others: (b) Inserting the catheter without preparation risks hypoxia and distress; (c) Continuous suction for a minute causes hypoxia and mucosal damage; (d) Suctioning is done when it is needed and not on a fixed sleep routine.

PGI Exam Trap: Suctioning is done without pre-oxygenation.

5-Second Recall: Pre-oxygenate and explain before suctioning.

PNC Exam Pearl: Limit each suction pass to about ten to fifteen seconds.

question: A nurse on the ward is about to move a heavy client from the bed to the chair and a mechanical lift is available. Which principle BEST explains why the nurse should use the lift?
option_1: Manual lifting is faster than using a mechanical lift
option_2: Safe client handling protects both the client and the nurse from injury
option_3: The mechanical lift can be used without any training
option_4: The client may prefer to be lifted by hand
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Safe client handling protects both the client and the nurse from injury

Clinical Rationale: Safe handling with the right equipment prevents musculoskeletal injury in the nurse and damage to the client.

Key Clue: moving a heavy client with a mechanical lift on the ward

Priority Principle: Safe patient handling

Why Not Others: (a) Speed is not the reason to avoid manual lifting; (c) A mechanical lift still needs training for safe use; (d) Client preference is considered but safety comes first.

PGI Exam Trap: Manual lifting is chosen for convenience.

5-Second Recall: Use the equipment and protect the back.

PNC Exam Pearl: Injury to nurses is a major cause of lost work time.

question: A 25-year-old woman in the postnatal period needs a perineal pad change after delivery. Which sequence is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Clean from the back to the front and then remove the pad
option_2: Remove the pad and then wash the hands
option_3: Wear gloves, remove the pad and clean from front to back
option_4: Apply the new pad before removing the soiled pad
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Wear gloves, remove the pad and clean from front to back

Clinical Rationale: Perineal care starts with hand hygiene and gloves and the cleaning is done from the front to the back to avoid infection.

Key Clue: sequence of perineal pad change in a woman after delivery

Priority Principle: Perineal care

Why Not Others: (a) Cleaning from back to front carries organisms to the perineum; (b) Hand hygiene is done before and not after the pad change; (d) The new pad is applied only after the soiled one is removed.

PGI Exam Trap: The cleaning direction is from back to front.

5-Second Recall: Clean the perineum from front to back.

PNC Exam Pearl: Change the pad at least every four hours.

question: A nurse manager on the ward notes that the same medication error has occurred three times and has harmed a patient. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Punish the nurse on each shift when the error occurs
option_2: Review the system with the staff and change the process to prevent it
option_3: Ignore the errors because no harm has resulted
option_4: Stop the use of similar drugs in the ward
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Review the system with the staff and change the process to prevent it

Clinical Rationale: Repeated errors usually point to a system problem, so the process is reviewed with the staff and changed to prevent recurrence.

Key Clue: same medication error repeated three times on the ward

Priority Principle: Quality improvement

Why Not Others: (a) Punishment encourages concealment and does not fix the system; (c) Ignoring the errors allows harm to occur later; (d) Stopping the use of similar drugs is not a practical or safe solution.

PGI Exam Trap: Only the individual is blamed for a system problem.

5-Second Recall: Repeated errors call for a system review.

PNC Exam Pearl: A just culture improves both reporting and safety.

question: A 45-year-old man on the ward with a chest drain has bubbling in the water seal chamber that increases when he coughs. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Air is leaking from the pleural space into the drain
option_2: The lung has fully re-expanded
option_3: The chest drain tube has become blocked
option_4: The suction is too low to work properly
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Air is leaking from the pleural space into the drain

Clinical Rationale: Increased bubbling in the water seal with coughing indicates an air leak from the pleural space into the drainage system.

Key Clue: bubbling in the water seal chamber on coughing in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Chest drain care

Why Not Others: (b) Full re-expansion stops the bubbling rather than increasing it; (c) A blocked drain stops the drainage and the bubbling; (d) Low suction would reduce and not increase the bubbling.

PGI Exam Trap: Bubbling is thought to mean healthy drainage.

5-Second Recall: Bubbling means air is entering the system.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check all the connections for a leak if the bubbling is continuous.

question: A mother brings her baby to the clinic and asks when the baby will FIRST smile at her. Which answer is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give?
option_1: At about one year of age
option_2: At birth
option_3: At about six months of age
option_4: At about six to eight weeks of age
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) At about six to eight weeks of age

Clinical Rationale: A social smile usually appears at about six to eight weeks of age as a response to a human face.

Key Clue: mother asking when a baby FIRST smiles

Priority Principle: Growth and development

Why Not Others: (a) One year is far too late for this milestone; (b) A social smile is not present at birth; (c) Six months is too late for the first social smile.

PGI Exam Trap: The social smile is expected much later than it appears.

5-Second Recall: The social smile appears at six to eight weeks.

PNC Exam Pearl: Note the parent's report of the smile during the visit.

question: A 75-year-old woman on the ward is to be turned in bed. Which action BEST prevents a shearing injury to her skin?
option_1: Leave the client in one position for a long time
option_2: Drag the client quickly across the sheet to save time
option_3: Pull the client by the arms to move her up
option_4: Use a draw sheet and lift rather than drag the client
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Use a draw sheet and lift rather than drag the client

Clinical Rationale: Using a draw sheet and lifting the client avoids the friction and shearing that damage the skin.

Key Clue: turning a woman on the ward safely to prevent a shearing injury

Priority Principle: Client positioning

Why Not Others: (a) Staying in one position increases the risk of pressure ulcers; (b) Dragging the client causes friction and a shearing injury; (c) Pulling by the arms can dislocate the shoulder and injure the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: The client is dragged to save time.

5-Second Recall: Lift with a draw sheet and do not drag.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two people turn a heavy client safely.

question: A mother brings her child to the clinic and is prescribed oral antibiotics. Which advice is the MOST appropriate to ensure that the full course is completed?
option_1: Complete the full course even after the child feels better
option_2: Stop the drug as soon as the fever settles
option_3: Give the drug when the fever becomes high
option_4: Double the dose to finish the course sooner
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Complete the full course even after the child feels better

Clinical Rationale: The full course of antibiotics is completed even after the symptoms improve so that the infection is fully treated.

Key Clue: child prescribed oral antibiotics by a mother at the clinic

Priority Principle: Antibiotic adherence

Why Not Others: (b) Stopping early allows the infection to relapse; (c) Irregular dosing leads to treatment failure; (d) Doubling the dose is unsafe and does not help.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is stopped once the fever settles.

5-Second Recall: Complete the full antibiotic course.

PNC Exam Pearl: Explain the schedule to the parent in simple words.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward has a serum potassium of 6.8 mEq/L with tall peaked T waves on the electrocardiogram. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Give potassium rich fruit juice at once
option_2: Stop the potassium intake and inform the doctor at once
option_3: Give a potassium supplement with the next dose
option_4: Wait for the next routine blood test
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the potassium intake and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A very high potassium with tall peaked T waves threatens the heart rhythm, so the potassium intake stops and treatment is prepared at once.

Key Clue: serum potassium of 6.8 mEq/L with tall peaked T waves in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Hyperkalaemia

Why Not Others: (a) Potassium rich juice would raise the level further; (c) A supplement would worsen the hyperkalaemia; (d) Waiting risks a fatal arrhythmia.

PGI Exam Trap: The electrocardiogram change is NOT linked to the potassium.

5-Second Recall: Tall peaked T waves mean hyperkalaemia.

PNC Exam Pearl: Calcium, insulin with glucose and resins lower the potassium.

question: A 70-year-old man on the ward who is receiving broad spectrum antibiotics develops watery diarrhoea with fever. Which organism is the MOST likely cause?
option_1: A fungal infection of the skin
option_2: A common cold virus that affects the nose and throat
option_3: Clostridium difficile after the normal gut flora is disturbed
option_4: A deficiency of vitamins in the diet
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Clostridium difficile after the normal gut flora is disturbed

Clinical Rationale: Broad spectrum antibiotics disturb the normal gut flora and allow Clostridium difficile to multiply and cause diarrhoea with fever.

Key Clue: watery diarrhoea with fever in a man on broad spectrum antibiotics

Priority Principle: Antibiotic associated diarrhoea

Why Not Others: (a) A fungal skin infection does not cause this diarrhoea; (b) A cold virus affects the respiratory tract and not the gut in this pattern; (d) A vitamin deficiency does not present with fever and watery stools.

PGI Exam Trap: Antibiotic associated diarrhoea is missed.

5-Second Recall: Antibiotics followed by diarrhoea means Clostridium difficile.

PNC Exam Pearl: Use antibiotics only when they are truly needed.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 30-year-old man on the ward is to receive electroconvulsive therapy. Which sequence is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Obtain consent, keep him fasting and give a short anaesthetic
option_2: Give the treatment without consent in every case
option_3: Allow a heavy meal just before the treatment
option_4: Give the treatment FIRST and obtain the consent afterwards
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Obtain consent, keep him fasting and give a short anaesthetic

Clinical Rationale: Electroconvulsive therapy follows informed consent and fasting before the short anaesthetic and the treatment itself.

Key Clue: sequence of electroconvulsive therapy for a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Electroconvulsive therapy

Why Not Others: (b) Consent is required except in the rare legal provisions; (c) A heavy meal before the anaesthetic risks aspiration; (d) Consent is taken before and not after the treatment.

PGI Exam Trap: Consent is considered unnecessary for this treatment.

5-Second Recall: Consent and fasting come before the anaesthetic.

PNC Exam Pearl: Explain the treatment well to reduce the fear.

question: A mother brings her baby to the clinic for immunisation, and the nurse finds that the square of the vaccine vial monitor is as dark as the circle. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Use the vaccine because it is within the expiry date
option_2: Discard the vaccine because it has been exposed to too much heat
option_3: Freeze the vaccine to make it safe again
option_4: Shake the vial well and use it quickly
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Discard the vaccine because it has been exposed to too much heat

Clinical Rationale: When the square of the vaccine vial monitor is as dark as the circle, the vaccine has been exposed to excessive heat and must be discarded.

Key Clue: vaccine vial monitor with a square as dark as the circle at the clinic

Priority Principle: Cold chain monitoring

Why Not Others: (a) The date does not matter once the monitor has changed fully; (c) Freezing does not restore a heat damaged vaccine; (d) Shaking does not reverse the heat damage.

PGI Exam Trap: The expiry date is relied upon despite the vial monitor.

5-Second Recall: A square as dark as the circle means discard.

PNC Exam Pearl: Read the vaccine vial monitor before every use.

question: A 50-year-old man on the ward who had surgery has a distended abdomen and has NOT passed flatus. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Insert a nasogastric tube without an order
option_2: Give a strong purgative at once
option_3: Assess the abdomen and encourage early ambulation
option_4: Restrict all the fluids
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Assess the abdomen and encourage early ambulation

Clinical Rationale: Paralytic ileus after surgery is FIRST assessed and managed with early ambulation and attention to the fluid and electrolyte state.

Key Clue: post operative distended abdomen with no flatus in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Post operative ileus

Why Not Others: (a) A nasogastric tube is inserted on medical orders and not at random; (b) A strong purgative can be harmful before the ileus is assessed; (d) Fluids are not restricted but managed carefully.

PGI Exam Trap: Bowel sounds are NOT assessed before treatment.

5-Second Recall: Assess and ambulate for post operative ileus.

PNC Exam Pearl: A silent abdomen with distension suggests paralytic ileus.

question: A 65-year-old man on the ward is prescribed an oral drug that is NOT available in the ward stock. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse?
option_1: Borrow the drug from another client's stock
option_2: Give a similar looking drug from the cupboard
option_3: Skip the dose and record it as given
option_4: Inform the doctor and the pharmacy rather than giving a substitute
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Inform the doctor and the pharmacy rather than giving a substitute

Clinical Rationale: An unavailable drug is reported to the doctor and the pharmacy and is never substituted or borrowed without an order.

Key Clue: prescribed oral drug NOT available in the ward stock

Priority Principle: Medication administration

Why Not Others: (a) Using another client's stock is not permitted; (b) Substituting a similar drug without an order is unsafe; (c) Skipping the dose and recording it falsely is unsafe and dishonest.

PGI Exam Trap: A substitute drug is given to avoid delay.

5-Second Recall: Report the shortage and do not substitute on your own.

PNC Exam Pearl: Accurate documentation protects the client and the nurse.

question: A nurse manager on the ward is preparing a nursing audit of the care given to a group of clients. Which sequence is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Collect the data before choosing the topic
option_2: Take corrective action before collecting any data
option_3: Set the standards after the data have been compared
option_4: Choose the topic, set the standards, collect the data and compare
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Choose the topic, set the standards, collect the data and compare

Clinical Rationale: A nursing audit follows a logical sequence that starts with the topic and the standards and ends in corrective action after the data are compared.

Key Clue: sequence of a nursing audit on the ward

Priority Principle: Nursing audit

Why Not Others: (a) The topic is chosen before the data collection begins; (b) Corrective action follows the comparison with the standards; (c) Standards are set before the data are collected.

PGI Exam Trap: Action is taken before the data are examined.

5-Second Recall: Topic, standards, data, comparison and action.

PNC Exam Pearl: A good audit always closes the loop with improvement.

question: A 70-year-old man on the ward is prescribed a suppository. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse?
option_1: Ask the client to bear down during the insertion
option_2: Insert the suppository dry into the anal canal
option_3: Lubricate it and insert it past the internal sphincter along the rectal wall
option_4: Ask the client to walk about at once after the insertion
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Lubricate it and insert it past the internal sphincter along the rectal wall

Clinical Rationale: A suppository is lubricated and inserted past the internal sphincter along the rectal wall so that it is retained and absorbed.

Key Clue: administration of a suppository to a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Rectal medication

Why Not Others: (a) Bearing down pushes the suppository out; (b) A dry suppository causes discomfort and may be expelled; (d) Walking at once encourages expulsion of the suppository.

PGI Exam Trap: The suppository is inserted only into the anal canal.

5-Second Recall: Insert past the internal sphincter and along the wall.

PNC Exam Pearl: Ask the client to remain in position for a few minutes.

question: A 40-year-old man on the ward with a head injury has a rising blood pressure with a falling pulse. Which change should the nurse attend to FIRST?
option_1: The change suggests a normal recovery after the injury
option_2: The rise suggests a rise in the pressure inside the skull
option_3: The change suggests simple anxiety and needs reassurance
option_4: The change suggests dehydration from a poor intake
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The rise suggests a rise in the pressure inside the skull

Clinical Rationale: A rising blood pressure with a falling pulse and a slowing respiration is the Cushing response of rising intracranial pressure.

Key Clue: rising blood pressure with a falling pulse after a head injury in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Intracranial pressure monitoring

Why Not Others: (a) The pattern is a warning sign and not a normal recovery; (c) Anxiety does not cause this specific pattern of signs; (d) Dehydration would not produce this combination.

PGI Exam Trap: The blood pressure rise is seen as a good sign.

5-Second Recall: Cushing response means rising pressure in the skull.

PNC Exam Pearl: Report the change at once and prepare for treatment.

question: A nurse manager on the ward is teaching new staff how to plan the care of a client. Which order of the steps of the nursing process is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation
option_2: Planning, assessment, evaluation, diagnosis and implementation
option_3: Diagnosis, planning, assessment, implementation and evaluation
option_4: Implementation, evaluation, assessment, diagnosis and planning
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation

Clinical Rationale: The nursing process begins with assessment and then proceeds to diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation.

Key Clue: teaching the steps of the nursing process on the ward

Priority Principle: Nursing process

Why Not Others: (b) Planning cannot come before the assessment and the diagnosis; (c) Assessment comes before the diagnosis is made; (d) Implementation follows the planning and not the reverse.

PGI Exam Trap: The steps of the nursing process are rearranged.

5-Second Recall: Assess, diagnose, plan, implement and evaluate.

PNC Exam Pearl: Evaluation feeds back into the assessment.

question: A nurse on the ward receives a splash of blood into the eyes while caring for a client. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Rub the eyes to remove the blood
option_2: Irrigate the eyes thoroughly with water or saline at once
option_3: Wait to see if any redness develops
option_4: Apply an antibiotic ointment before washing
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Irrigate the eyes thoroughly with water or saline at once

Clinical Rationale: A blood splash to the eyes is irrigated at once with clean water or saline to reduce the exposure.

Key Clue: splash of blood into the eyes of a nurse caring for a client

Priority Principle: Post exposure management

Why Not Others: (a) Rubbing the eyes can injure the surface and does not help; (c) Waiting allows the organisms to stay in contact; (d) Ointment is applied after the irrigation and not before.

PGI Exam Trap: Eye irrigation is delayed until redness appears.

5-Second Recall: Irrigate the eyes at once after a blood splash.

PNC Exam Pearl: Report the exposure and follow the protocol for testing.

question: A staff nurse on the ward is teaching a student how to prepare the instruments used for a client. Which statement about sterilisation and disinfection is the MOST appropriate for the student to remember?
option_1: Sterilisation destroys all the microorganisms including the spores
option_2: Disinfection destroys all the spores as well
option_3: Sterilisation removes the dust but NOT the organisms
option_4: Disinfection and sterilisation mean the same thing
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Sterilisation destroys all the microorganisms including the spores

Clinical Rationale: Sterilisation kills all the microorganisms including the bacterial spores while disinfection destroys the pathogens on inanimate objects.

Key Clue: difference between sterilisation and disinfection in the ward

Priority Principle: Infection control

Why Not Others: (b) Disinfection does not reliably destroy the spores; (c) Sterilisation destroys the spores as well and not only the dust; (d) The two terms describe different processes.

PGI Exam Trap: Disinfection is believed to destroy the spores.

5-Second Recall: Sterilisation includes the spores and disinfection does not.

PNC Exam Pearl: Use sterilisation for things that enter the body.

question: A 20-year-old man on the ward with a below knee plaster cast has severe pain that is NOT relieved by the prescribed analgesic. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Elevate the limb and review the client in the morning
option_2: Give a second dose of the analgesic and record it
option_3: Reassure the client that the pain is expected
option_4: Assess the neurovascular status and inform the doctor promptly
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Assess the neurovascular status and inform the doctor promptly

Clinical Rationale: Unrelieved pain in a cast may mean impaired circulation or compartment syndrome, so the neurovascular status is assessed and the doctor informed.

Key Clue: cast pain NOT relieved by the prescribed analgesic in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Compartment syndrome

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting until the morning risks permanent damage; (b) A second analgesic dose masks the warning sign; (c) Treating the pain as expected delays the diagnosis.

PGI Exam Trap: Severe cast pain is treated as normal.

5-Second Recall: Pain out of proportion to the injury means compartment syndrome.

PNC Exam Pearl: Loosen the bandage and report the findings at once.

question: A 25-year-old woman who attends the clinic has anaemia. Which advice about food is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Take white bread with jam for breakfast
option_2: Take plain rice with butter at each meal
option_3: Take green leafy vegetables with a source of vitamin C
option_4: Take tea with biscuits in the evening
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Take green leafy vegetables with a source of vitamin C

Clinical Rationale: Green leafy vegetables provide iron and vitamin C helps the body to absorb it.

Key Clue: woman with anaemia who attends the clinic

Priority Principle: Nutrition in anaemia

Why Not Others: (a) White bread with jam is poor in iron; (b) Rice with butter provides energy but very little iron; (d) Tea with biscuits provides little iron and the tannins reduce absorption.

PGI Exam Trap: Iron rich foods are taken without vitamin C.

5-Second Recall: Iron food with vitamin C improves absorption.

PNC Exam Pearl: Avoid tea with iron rich meals.

question: A 70-year-old man on the ward with a urinary catheter develops cloudy urine with a strong smell. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Increase the fluids and inform the doctor about the infection
option_2: Irrigate the catheter with a strong antiseptic
option_3: Remove the catheter at once without an order
option_4: Clamp the catheter to rest the bladder
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Increase the fluids and inform the doctor about the infection

Clinical Rationale: Cloudy smelly urine suggests a urinary tract infection, so the fluids are increased and the doctor is informed for treatment.

Key Clue: cloudy urine with a strong smell in a man on the ward with a catheter

Priority Principle: Catheter associated infection

Why Not Others: (b) Routine irrigation with a strong antiseptic is not advised; (c) Removing the catheter needs a medical order; (d) Clamping the catheter retains the infected urine.

PGI Exam Trap: The catheter is removed without any order.

5-Second Recall: Cloudy smelly urine means a urinary infection.

PNC Exam Pearl: Good catheter care and adequate fluids prevent infection.

question: A 25-year-old woman in labour on the ward has her progress charted on a partogram. Which statement about the partogram is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It records the weight of the mother after delivery
option_2: It records the progress of labour against time and detects delay early
option_3: It records the immunisation details of the baby
option_4: It records the family history of the mother in detail
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It records the progress of labour against time and detects delay early

Clinical Rationale: A partogram charts the dilatation, the descent and the vital signs of labour over time so that any delay is recognised early.

Key Clue: woman in labour on the ward with the progress charted on a partogram

Priority Principle: Monitoring of labour

Why Not Others: (a) The partogram records the progress of labour and not the weight; (c) Immunisation details are recorded after the birth and not on the partogram; (d) The family history is taken in the antenatal period.

PGI Exam Trap: The partogram is seen as a general record sheet.

5-Second Recall: The partogram shows the progress of labour against time.

PNC Exam Pearl: A partogram in use helps to prevent prolonged labour.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 45-year-old man on the ward with acute pancreatitis has severe pain. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Encourage the client to walk about briskly
option_2: Give a fatty meal to test the digestion
option_3: Keep him nil by mouth and give the prescribed analgesia
option_4: Give aspirin for the pain
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep him nil by mouth and give the prescribed analgesia

Clinical Rationale: Acute pancreatitis is managed by resting the pancreas through keeping the client nil by mouth and giving the prescribed analgesia.

Key Clue: severe pain in acute pancreatitis in a man on the ward

Priority Principle: Acute pancreatitis

Why Not Others: (a) Brisk walking increases the pain and the pancreatic stimulation; (b) A fatty meal stimulates the pancreas and worsens the pain; (d) Aspirin is not the analgesic of choice in this condition.

PGI Exam Trap: Food is given to test the pancreatic function.

5-Second Recall: Nil by mouth and analgesia for acute pancreatitis.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watch the serum amylase and the blood sugar.

question: A 65-year-old man on the ward with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease becomes drowsy after oxygen at a high flow rate. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Ask the client to breathe faster
option_2: Increase the oxygen further to improve the drowsiness
option_3: Stop all the oxygen at once
option_4: Reduce the oxygen to the prescribed low rate
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Reduce the oxygen to the prescribed low rate

Clinical Rationale: Drowsiness in a chronic carbon dioxide retainer during oxygen therapy signals carbon dioxide retention, so the flow is reduced to the prescribed level and the doctor is informed.

Key Clue: drowsy man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on high flow oxygen

Priority Principle: Oxygen therapy in chronic lung disease

Why Not Others: (a) Asking the client to breathe faster does not correct the problem; (b) More oxygen would deepen the carbon dioxide retention; (c) Stopping the oxygen abruptly worsens the hypoxia.

PGI Exam Trap: Drowsiness is treated as a need for more oxygen.

5-Second Recall: Reduce the flow and report in carbon dioxide retainers.

PNC Exam Pearl: Use controlled low flow oxygen in chronic lung disease.

question: A 3-year-old child is brought to the clinic with a foreign body in the nose. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the child to breathe through the mouth and assess the obstruction
option_2: Ask the child to blow the nose forcefully at once
option_3: Remove the object with any instrument that is available
option_4: Push the object further in to see it clearly
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Ask the child to breathe through the mouth and assess the obstruction

Clinical Rationale: The airway is kept clear through the mouth and the obstruction is assessed before any attempt at removal is made.

Key Clue: child with a foreign body in the nose brought to the clinic

Priority Principle: Foreign body in the nose

Why Not Others: (b) Forceful blowing can push the object into the airway; (c) Removing with a random instrument can injure the child; (d) Pushing the object further risks aspiration.

PGI Exam Trap: The object is removed without any assessment.

5-Second Recall: Assess first and keep the airway clear.

PNC Exam Pearl: Refer to the doctor if removal is difficult.

question: A 55-year-old man on the ward is being helped out of bed for the FIRST time after surgery. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Raise the bed to the highest position before helping
option_2: Pull him upright quickly to save time
option_3: Ask him to walk unaided at once
option_4: Let him sit at the edge of the bed FIRST and then stand with support
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Let him sit at the edge of the bed FIRST and then stand with support

Clinical Rationale: Sitting at the edge of the bed FIRST allows the circulation to adjust and reduces the risk of fainting.

Key Clue: helping a post operative man on the ward out of bed for the FIRST time

Priority Principle: Mobilising the client

Why Not Others: (a) The bed is kept at a safe low height for the transfer; (b) Pulling the client up quickly causes dizziness and falls; (c) Walking unaided risks a fall on the first attempt.

PGI Exam Trap: The client is stood up at once without sitting FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Sit first and then stand with support.

PNC Exam Pearl: Have two helpers for the first ambulation.

question: A nurse on the ward is about to draw up a drug for a client and sees particles floating in the solution of the ampoule. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Warm the ampoule and then use it quickly
option_2: Shake the ampoule well and use the solution
option_3: Discard the ampoule because the solution is NOT fit for injection
option_4: Filter the solution with cotton and inject it
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Discard the ampoule because the solution is NOT fit for injection

Clinical Rationale: A solution with visible particles must be discarded and never injected because it may cause an embolism or an adverse reaction.

Key Clue: ampoule of a drug with particles in the solution in the ward

Priority Principle: Safe injection practice

Why Not Others: (a) Warming the ampoule does not make the solution safe; (b) Shaking does not remove the particles and the solution stays unsafe; (d) Cotton is not a sterile filter and cannot make the solution safe.

PGI Exam Trap: Particles are ignored in a needed drug.

5-Second Recall: Inspect the solution before every injection.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the colour and the clarity of every injectable.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward who is receiving a nasogastric feed develops diarrhoea. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Stop all the feeds permanently
option_2: Review the rate and the concentration of the feed
option_3: Give an antidiarrhoeal drug at once
option_4: Give a large bolus of the feed to settle the stomach
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Review the rate and the concentration of the feed

Clinical Rationale: Diarrhoea during enteral feeding commonly follows a rapid rate or a high concentration of the feed, which are reviewed FIRST.

Key Clue: diarrhoea in a man on the ward receiving a nasogastric feed

Priority Principle: Enteral feeding complications

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping the feeds permanently is not needed and causes malnutrition; (c) An antidiarrhoeal drug does not correct the feeding problem; (d) A large bolus of feed would worsen the diarrhoea.

PGI Exam Trap: The diarrhoea is treated without looking at the feed.

5-Second Recall: Review the rate and the strength of the feed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the feed temperature and the hygiene of preparation.

question: A community health nurse visits a village where a mother reports that several children have had fever. Which action is the MOST appropriate to prevent mosquito borne disease?
option_1: Remove the standing water and use measures to protect from bites
option_2: Build more houses for the families in the village
option_3: Open more shops for the people of the village
option_4: Increase the number of buses that go to the town
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Remove the standing water and use measures to protect from bites

Clinical Rationale: Source reduction of the breeding places together with protection from bites is the basis for preventing mosquito borne diseases.

Key Clue: prevention of mosquito borne diseases in a village

Priority Principle: Vector control

Why Not Others: (b) More houses do not reduce the mosquitoes; (c) More shops have no effect on the mosquito population; (d) More buses do not prevent the vector borne disease.

PGI Exam Trap: The breeding places are left untouched.

5-Second Recall: Remove the standing water and protect from bites.

PNC Exam Pearl: Community participation makes vector control lasting.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 40-year-old man who comes to the clinic must choose between two treatments. Which action BEST respects his autonomy?
option_1: Decide for him in order to save time
option_2: Explain the options and allow him to make the final decision
option_3: Tell him that there is a single option for the problem
option_4: Ask the family to decide without telling him
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Explain the options and allow him to make the final decision

Clinical Rationale: Autonomy means the client is informed of the options and is free to make the final choice about their care.

Key Clue: man at the clinic who must choose between two treatments

Priority Principle: Principles of ethics

Why Not Others: (a) Deciding for the client removes the right of the client to choose; (c) Hiding the options is not honest and removes the choice; (d) Deciding without the knowledge of the client violates autonomy.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse decides in the BEST interest of the client without consent.

5-Second Recall: Autonomy is the right of the client to choose.

PNC Exam Pearl: Informed choice is the basis of ethical care.

question: A 35-year-old woman on the ward needs a midstream urine specimen. Which sequence is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Collect the specimen after the whole bladder is emptied
option_2: Collect the FIRST part of the urine in the container
option_3: Clean the area, discard the FIRST urine and collect the middle portion
option_4: Collect the specimen from the bedpan
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Clean the area, discard the FIRST urine and collect the middle portion

Clinical Rationale: A midstream specimen follows cleaning and the discard of the FIRST urine so that the middle portion is collected cleanly.

Key Clue: collecting a midstream urine specimen from a woman on the ward

Priority Principle: Specimen collection

Why Not Others: (a) The last portion is not the midstream specimen; (b) The first portion contains the organisms from the urethra; (d) A specimen from the bedpan is contaminated.

PGI Exam Trap: The FIRST urine is collected as the specimen.

5-Second Recall: Discard the first part and collect the middle.

PNC Exam Pearl: Send the specimen to the laboratory without delay.

question: A 70-year-old woman on the ward is to have an occupied bed made. Which sequence is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Keep the side rails down while the client is turned
option_2: Place the clean linen under the soiled linen and leave it there
option_3: Remove the linen with the client on the same side the whole time
option_4: Raise the bed, remove the soiled linen and roll the client to the side
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Raise the bed, remove the soiled linen and roll the client to the side

Clinical Rationale: An occupied bed is made with the bed raised and the client rolled safely from side to side as the clean linen is placed.

Key Clue: making an occupied bed for a woman on the ward

Priority Principle: Bed making

Why Not Others: (a) The side rail is kept up on the side away from the nurse; (b) The clean linen is not left under the soiled linen; (c) The client is turned from side to side during the procedure.

PGI Exam Trap: The rails are left down while the client is turned.

5-Second Recall: Raise the bed and keep the far rail up.

PNC Exam Pearl: Do not turn your back on a client in bed.

question: A community health nurse visits a village where a mother reports that many people have fever with calf pain and a rapid pulse, and Aedes larvae are found in the stored water. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Report the outbreak, remove the breeding sources and step up surveillance
option_2: Give painkillers to all and wait for the fever to settle
option_3: Advise the people to store more water
option_4: Spray insecticide once and close the investigation
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Report the outbreak, remove the breeding sources and step up surveillance

Clinical Rationale: Fever with calf pain and a rapid pulse along with Aedes larvae suggests dengue, so the case is reported, the breeding sources are removed and the surveillance is started.

Key Clue: fever with calf pain and rapid pulse with Aedes larvae in stored water in a village

Priority Principle: Dengue outbreak control

Why Not Others: (b) Painkillers alone do not control the outbreak; (c) Storing more water increases the breeding sites; (d) One spraying is not enough and the investigation must continue.

PGI Exam Trap: The outbreak is managed with painkillers alone.

5-Second Recall: Dengue control means source reduction and surveillance.

PNC Exam Pearl: Warn the family about warning signs like bleeding.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 25-year-old woman on the ward reports regular painful contractions. Which statement about the onset of labour is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Any pain in the abdomen marks the onset of labour
option_2: Regular painful contractions with a change in the cervix mark the onset
option_3: A show by itself means that labour has begun
option_4: Rupture of the membranes by itself means that labour has begun
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Regular painful contractions with a change in the cervix mark the onset

Clinical Rationale: True labour is marked by regular painful contractions along with the effacement and the progressive dilatation of the cervix.

Key Clue: woman on the ward with regular painful contractions

Priority Principle: Onset of labour

Why Not Others: (a) Abdominal pain alone can have many other causes; (c) A show may occur before true labour begins; (d) The membranes can rupture without labour and then need induction.

PGI Exam Trap: Any one sign is taken as the onset of labour.

5-Second Recall: Regular contractions with a cervical change mean true labour.

PNC Exam Pearl: False labour pains do not change the cervix.

question: A 45-year-old man on the ward has a peptic ulcer. Which advice is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Drink strong coffee to reduce the acid
option_2: Take a large meal at night before sleeping
option_3: Avoid spicy food, alcohol and smoking and take the drugs
option_4: Stop the antacid drug once the pain settles
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Avoid spicy food, alcohol and smoking and take the drugs

Clinical Rationale: Peptic ulcer care includes avoiding the irritants such as spicy food, alcohol and smoking and taking the prescribed drugs regularly.

Key Clue: man on the ward with a peptic ulcer

Priority Principle: Peptic ulcer care

Why Not Others: (a) Strong coffee increases the acid secretion; (b) A large night meal increases the acid secretion and the pain; (d) The drugs are completed as prescribed and not stopped early.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is treated and the irritants are ignored.

5-Second Recall: Avoid the irritants and take the drugs regularly.

PNC Exam Pearl: Screen for Helicobacter pylori infection.

question: A 35-year-old man who is admitted to the ward asks about his relationship with the nursing staff. Which statement about the nurse-client relationship is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It has no fixed boundaries and depends on the nurse
option_2: It continues as a personal friendship after discharge
option_3: It begins with the nurse sharing personal problems
option_4: It is a goal directed relationship that is time limited
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It is a goal directed relationship that is time limited

Clinical Rationale: The therapeutic nurse-client relationship is purposeful and time limited and it ends once the needs of the client have been met.

Key Clue: man admitted to the ward who asks about the relationship with the nursing staff

Priority Principle: Therapeutic relationship

Why Not Others: (a) The relationship has clear professional boundaries; (b) A professional relationship does not continue as a personal friendship; (c) The nurse does not burden the client with personal problems.

PGI Exam Trap: The relationship is treated as a friendship.

5-Second Recall: Therapeutic relationships are goal directed and time limited.

PNC Exam Pearl: Maintain boundaries to keep the trust intact.
